Subject: Post-call: Performance/SLO requirements for Private VPC - Acme Retail

Hi James / Sara —

Thanks again for the time on today's call. Quick recap and the concrete next steps so we can get the performance qualification started for your Private/VPC deployment. We captured action items for both sides below.

High-level performance targets discussed
- Latency: p95 generation latency target <= 200 ms (end-to-end, client -> app -> model -> response)
- Throughput: steady-state 500 RPS with 50 concurrent model sessions
- Concurrency: up to 100 concurrent short-lived sessions during peaks; typical burst to 200 for 2–3 minutes acceptable
- Streaming: token streaming required for chat flows; need sustained stream of ~20 tokens/sec per session at peak

Network / VPC considerations we need to validate
- Preferred connectivity: VPC Peering (preferred) vs Site-to-Site VPN (fallback)
- Egress: allow outbound to Redwood egress IP ranges (we'll provide) and open return path
- Internal latency budget: want app-to-inference-proxy <= 30–50 ms ideally to meet end-to-end SLOs
- MTU, keepalive, and idle timeouts can affect streaming—please confirm NAT / LB timeouts

Attached: Redwood network checklist + initial SLO worksheet (stub files)

Next steps / owners
- Redwood (Aditya/Dev): provide IP ranges, peering instructions, and a short checklist for traceroute/iperf commands to run (by Tue 3/10)
- Acme (James/Sara): confirm whether you can do VPC peering and share a contact for your network engineer + preferred maintenance window (by Wed 3/11)
- Agree on a test plan for a staged throughput run once peering is up (schedule after peering confirmed)

If anything above is off from what you expect, flag it here and we'll correct. Otherwise I'll schedule a 30-min network/SE session with Dev and your network engineer for next week.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — good summary. A few clarifications from our side:
- We can do VPC peering; prefer peering into our us-east-1 account. Will need the IP ranges and peering template from Redwood.
- The 200 ms p95 target is ambitious but reasonable if internal network latency is kept low. Our network team estimates app->inference path is typically 20–40 ms within the VPC, but we need your SE to validate expected added latency for the proxy -> GPU host.
- For streaming, our clients expect low jitter; please confirm keepalive / idle timeouts and whether Redwood does TLS termination on your side or will we terminate at our edge?

I've looped in Sara (network lead) — Sara, can you share an initial availability for a short network call this week?

- James

Hi Sara / James — happy to jump in. A few technical clarifications and immediate asks so we can size the test properly: 

Immediate items we need from Acme (please provide before the network session):
- CIDR(s) you plan to peer with and a contact for the peering request
- Expected request size distribution (mean tokens / payload size) and typical requests per session
- Whether you want TLS terminated at your edge (we can support both). If you terminate at your edge, we'll use mTLS to the inference proxy.

Suggested test checklist (quick commands to run from an app host in your VPC):
- traceroute -n <redwood-proxy-ip>
- mtr --report <redwood-proxy-ip>
- iperf3 -c <redwood-iperf-server> -t 30 (run both directions)
- capture 1-min p95 latency for HTTP chunked streaming at small token payloads

Latency budget assumptions (for discussion on call):
- app -> inference proxy (within VPC): target <= 30 ms (p95)
- inference proxy -> GPU host (Redwood-managed/peered): expected additional 60–120 ms depending on model size and token generation profile
- end-to-end target p95 <= 200 ms requires optimizing batching and enabling KV cache where possible

Notes on streaming and timeouts:
- Idle timeout: please ensure LB/NGINX idle timeout is >= 120s to avoid cutting long-lived streams; otherwise we recommend client-side reconnect logic
- Keepalive: enable TCP keepalive at 30s if possible to keep NAT mappings stable for streaming flows

I'll draft a short network runbook and share by tomorrow. If you can share CIDRs and a network contact, we can send the peering template and sample CloudFormation/TF snippet.

Thanks — Dev
